added.title: Director, Tegra Firmware
added.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are searching for a skilled technical and organizational leader to guide foundational firmware development for Tegra CPU and system-on-chip platforms. Tegra combines high-performance CPUs with NVIDIA GPUs and specialized accelerators to power autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, edge AI, and other demanding applications. We are building the foundational firmware that brings each new generation of Tegra silicon to life! You will guide globally distributed teams responsible for CPU and SoC initialization, secure boot, system control, safety services, confidential computing, and production diagnostics. This position requires extensive embedded-systems expertise, strong architectural judgment, and a history of delivering production firmware across multiple silicon generations.

What You’ll Be Doing

Lead and grow globally distributed firmware teams and engineering managers.
Own delivery from architecture and pre-silicon development through bring-up, production, and long-term support.
Direct development of CPU boot, memory and coherency initialization, multicore startup, power-state transitions, confidential compute, and OS handoff.
Partner with CPU, SoC, hardware, verification, OS, DRIVE OS, safety, security, and product teams on integrated platform delivery.
Drive pre-silicon readiness, silicon bring-up, fault injection, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and development automation.
Lead firmware execution for automotive and industrial programs aligned with ISO 26262, IEC 61508, ISO/SAE 21434, and applicable certification requirements.
Oversee safety and security activities such as requirements traceability, FMEA, FTA, threat analysis, secure design reviews, verification evidence, and assessor engagement.
Work with OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, industrial customers, and ecosystem partners to resolve technical and delivery challenges.

What We Need To See

BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field—or equivalent experience.
12+ overall years of experience in embedded firmware, system software, or low-level platform software.
7+ years of engineering leadership experience, including leading managers or distributed teams.
Proven success delivering complex CPU or SoC firmware from architecture through production.
Deep understanding of CPUs, multicore systems, caches, coherency, memory, interrupts, power management, and hardware-software interfaces.
Strong knowledge of bare-metal or real-time firmware, bootloaders, embedded operating systems, Linux internals, and hardware bring-up.
Experience with heterogeneous SoCs containing CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, security processors, or system-control microcontrollers.
Experience with pre-silicon development, post-silicon debugging, failure analysis, and in-field diagnostic processes.
Strong understanding of firmware quality, reliability, secure development, and product lifecycle management.
Excellent technical judgment, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience with NVIDIA Tegra or another complex automotive, robotics, industrial, or edge-computing SoC.
Expertise in ARM Trusted Firmware, UEFI, bootloaders, secure monitors, RTOS platforms, or system-control processors.
Knowledge of safety analysis, fault-tolerant architecture, safety cases, or Safety Element out of Context development.
Experience with threat modeling, hardware roots of trust, secure and measured boot, attestation, key management, or secure update.
A record of influencing CPU or SoC architecture across multiple silicon generations.

Who We Are:

Aurelius Systems is a VC backed defense tech startup building autonomous, edge deployed directed energy systems for counter-UAS. We build laser weapons to shoot down drones.

We're a small team of engineers, former US military operators, and subject matter experts scaling America's directed energy dominance. The first cost effective, reliable and robust laser weapon system.

Our namesake isn't an accident. Marcus Aurelius wrote about doing the work in front of you, every day, without excuses. Henry Ford didn't wait for permission to reinvent manufacturing. That's how we operate, small team, unreasonable output, no hiding behind the unachievable.

In addition to our San Francisco lab, we've opened a Detroit manufacturing hub and we field test weekly on our own 400-acre private range.

The Role and Your Impact:

We need an Engineering Director to own the path from R&D to production across the whole system. You'll lead multiple engineering disciplines from software, firmware, controls, hardware integration, test, and drive the hard handoff from a thing that works in the lab to a thing that survives downrange and gets built at volume. This is the person who turns a demonstrator into a weapon system. You'll set technical direction, and run the org that executes it.

What You'll Own:

Technical direction across software, firmware, controls, hardware integration, and test for the full system
The R&D to production transition and authority architecture taking subsystems from prototype through field-ready and manufacturable
Multi-team execution under ambiguous requirements, charting clear guidance and seeing projects through delivery
Field testing leadership, from test article design through scoring system performance in non-lab conditions
Building and scaling the engineering org from hiring, structure, and growing high-performing teams from the ground up
Customer and program interface, translating mission requirements into engineering execution
The technical bar across the team. An engineer first, and leader second. You raise it by how you work, not by what you say

What We're Looking For:

12+ years in engineering with significant leadership of multi-disciplinary technical teams
Track record taking complex hardware/software systems from R&D through production or field deployment
Experience leading across disciplines — you don't have to be the deepest in every domain, but you have to earn the respect of engineers who are
Demonstrated ability to scale teams and turn dysfunction or ambiguity into high-performing execution
Comfort operating hands-on in a lab and on a test range, not just in planning tools

Nice to Haves:

Active or recent DoD security clearance
Directed energy or high energy laser weapon system experience
Experience standing up engineering processes and tooling for a scaling org
US military background or deep experience working with military end users
Track record of hiring and growing senior technical talent

Education:

Advanced degree in a relevant engineering or physical science field is a plus, but track record beats credentials. No specific degree required.

How You Operate:

Extreme bias for action. You'd rather solve it now than schedule a meeting about it
You handle problems before they hit anyone's inbox
Comfortable with ambiguity and fast iteration in a startup environment
Clear communicator across engineering, leadership, customers, and the range
Self directed. You identify what needs to happen next and do it without being told

Why Join Aurelius Systems?

Build more in 1 month than most people build in 1 year. We field test weekly. Your work makes the whole team faster.
Career velocity is real. At ~10 engineers, there are no layers between you and impact.
Work on a problem that actually matters. Small cheap drones are changing warfare. Our laser systems are the asymmetric answer — infinite magazine, near zero cost per shot, scalable to every base, border, facility, and truck.
Join the densest defense startup ecosystem in the country. California is where the next generation of defense companies are being built.

How We Work:

Core hours are Monday through Friday, 9 to 6. When we're sprinting toward a demo or field test, the team ramps up — nights, weekends, whatever it takes to ship. When the sprint lands, we ramp down. We don't manufacture intensity for show.

Flexible 18 days PTO + 5 sick days
Travel to field test events and range days
Covered daily lunches and office snacks + drinks
E-bike / scooter stipend (Up to $500)
Direct access to leadership and real ownership over your work

added.title: Senior Engineering Manager, API Catalog
added.description:
Who Are We?

Postman is the world’s leading API platform, used by more than 45 million+ developers and 500,000 organizations, including 98% of the Fortune 500. Postman is helping developers and professionals across the globe build the API-first world by simplifying each step of the API lifecycle and streamlining collaboration—enabling users to create better APIs, faster.

The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Boston, New York, Austin, Tokyo, London, and Bangalore - where Postman was founded. Postman is privately held, with funding from Battery Ventures, BOND, Coatue, CRV, Insight Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. Learn more at postman.com or connect with Postman on X via @getpostman.

P.S: We highly recommend reading The "API-First World" graphic novel to understand the bigger picture and our vision at Postman.

The Opportunity

A large enterprise runs hundreds of services across multiple cloud accounts, multiple gateways, several repository hosts, and a mix of cloud and on-prem infrastructure. Nobody can produce a complete list. Postman's API Catalog is the system of record that can: it connects to where APIs actually live, brings them into a single inventory, and gives platform teams the means to govern them — ownership, environments, specification compliance, and evidence that release gates were met.

What's ahead is: turning a product that works into the system of record that a large platform organization standardizes on company-wide. That means carrying estates an order of magnitude larger than today's, reaching every environment and every gateway an enterprise actually runs, and becoming the control plane through which API governance happens rather than one more inventory somebody has to maintain.

We're hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to own the engineering behind it. You'll lead a small, senior, US-based team, and you'll spend a meaningful share of your time landing work that crosses team boundaries — because most of what this roadmap needs, this team does not build alone.

What This Team Owns

Service discovery and ingestion breadth.
Connecting to the systems where APIs are defined and deployed — repository providers across cloud and self-hosted, cloud API gateways, and clusters. Breadth is the growth axis: each provider we support is an enterprise we can serve.

Enterprise reporting and governance evidence.
Test and CI-pipeline reporting, specification linting, and the records enterprises use to prove a release met its gates. Trust is the product here; a number a customer can't reconcile is worse than no number at all.

Gateway federation.
Large organizations don't run one gateway; they run several, from different vendors, across many accounts, often with different teams owning each. Federating that estate into a single governed view — and doing it without asking customers to reorganize around us — is one of the defining technical problems of this product's next phase.

Event-driven API support.
Extending the catalog beyond request/response to event technologies — beginning with Kafka, end to end from client through specification and governance into the catalog.

Product maturity, reliability, and telemetry.
Metrics you can trust as a single source of truth, a support flow that doesn't consume the roadmap, and datastore reliability that doesn't produce customer-visible incidents. This is treated as a first-class investment area, not overhead.

The API Catalog owns the system of record: how services are discovered, ingested, federated, linked to environments, governed, and reported on.

What You'll Do

Lead a senior team

Manage, coach, and grow a team of experienced engineers, some of whom hold institutional knowledge that predates you. The work is surfacing gaps and raising the bar, then letting senior engineers own the fix.
Hire deliberately as the team grows, and set a clear technical bar in the process.
Set explicit goals, give direct feedback, and keep the team's work legible to the rest of the organization.
Reduce single-owner concentration on critical systems. Spread context deliberately rather than letting it pool in one person.

Land work that crosses team boundaries

This deserves its own section because it is the largest determinant of whether this role succeeds.

Most of what the catalog ships depends on teams you don't manage — specification tooling, the API client, the integrations and ecosystem teams that own provider connectivity, and shared platform services. You'll need to secure commitments, sequence around other teams' plans, and unblock reviews without escalating every time.
Own the seams: define the contracts between the catalog and its dependencies clearly enough that both sides can move independently.
Be honest and early about which commitments are genuinely at the mercy of another team's roadmap, and bring options rather than only the blocker.

Own the technical direction

Drive architecture and execution across ingestion, federation, the service model, and the reporting and deployment data layers, with correctness, multi-tenant isolation, and cost-per-tenant as design constraints rather than afterthoughts.
Set the quality bar for reporting accuracy and build the measurement to know whether you're meeting it. A number a customer can't reconcile is worse than no number.
Treat on-prem and self-managed deployments as a first-class variant of every connector, not a port.
Hold the line on engineering fundamentals — design review, testing, safe staged rollout, and instrumentation of the team's own services.

Own delivery

Own the API Catalog engineering roadmap and its tradeoffs, balancing enterprise commitments, connector breadth, and debt in systems that predate the current product direction.
Break large initiatives into milestones that ship incrementally and can be evaluated on the way. Several of this team's initiatives will mature beyond a single quarter; plan accordingly.
Own production reliability and the support burden, and treat recurring toil as a design problem rather than a staffing one.

What We're Looking For

Must have

10+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years leading engineering teams.
Depth you can prove on a hard technical problem you personally solved — a system you designed and debugged yourself, not a project you oversaw. We will ask you to go deep on this.
- Experience taking a validated product from 1→10 — scaling something that already had customers into something a large organization standardizes on. This is not a 0→1 role; the interesting problems here are breadth, scale, and trust rather than product discovery.
Production ownership of an enterprise integration surface at breadth — many third-party providers, each with its own authentication, rate limits, permission model, and cloud-versus-self-hosted differences. You've felt the maintenance cost of the tenth connector.
Demonstrated ability to ship work that depends on teams you don't manage, in an organization where those teams have their own roadmaps.
Experience leading a senior-heavy team, where the job was elevating strong engineers rather than directing junior ones.
Multi-tenant enterprise SaaS, including customers with on-prem or self-managed infrastructure and real compliance requirements.
Full lifecycle ownership from design through production support.
Clear, economical communication with engineers, executives, and customers. You'll be in front of all three.

Nice to have

API gateway technologies and cloud provider control-plane APIs (AWS, GCP, Azure), plus Kubernetes.
CI/CD systems and developer workflow tooling — you understand what it takes for a team to accept a new gate in their pipeline.
Analytical datastores supporting customer-facing reporting (ClickHouse or similar), including the operational reality of them.
Event-driven and asynchronous API technologies, particularly Kafka.
Governance, audit, or compliance reporting for enterprise buyers.

The reasonably estimated base salary for this role ranges from $280,000 to $320,000, plus a competitive equity package. Actual compensation is based on the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience.

What Else?

In addition to Postman's pay-on-performance philosophy, and a flexible schedule working with a fun, collaborative team, Postman offers a comprehensive set of benefits, including full medical coverage, flexible PTO, wellness reimbursement, and a monthly lunch stipend. Along with that, our wellness programs will help you stay in the best of your physical and mental health. Our frequent and fascinating team-building events will keep you connected, while our donation-matching program can support the causes you care about. We’re building a long-term company with an inclusive culture where everyone can be the best version of themselves.

At Postman we value in person collaboration. We are in office 5 days a week for all roles based out of our hubs in San Francisco Bay Area, Boston, Austin, New York City, Tokyo and London. For roles based in Bangalore, employees currently work in the office three days a week and will transition to five days per week by the end of the year. We were thoughtful in our approach which is based on collaboration and grounded in feedback from our workforce, leadership team, and peers. The benefits of our in office model will be shared knowledge, brainstorming sessions, communication, and building trust in-person that cannot be replicated via zoom.

Our Values

At Postman, we create with the same curiosity that we see in our users. We value transparency and honest communication about not only successes, but also failures. In our work, we focus on specific goals that add up to a larger vision. Our inclusive work culture ensures that everyone is valued equally as important pieces of our final product. We are dedicated to delivering the best products we can.

Systems Engineering

Position Overview

The Senior Director, Lifecycle Engineering is the enterprise leader for the systems, data, and operating model that governs equipment digital thread from product definition through procurement, manufacture, logistics, commissioning and handover into asset, Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS)/ Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) and data-centre maintenance operations.

The role sets the lifecycle engineering strategy, investment portfolio, architecture, and governance required to establish a scalable equipment digital thread: a canonical equipment and asset master, controlled product, configuration, Bill of Materials (BOM), and technical-documentation data, a single asset identity across system boundaries, and CMMS/EAM capabilities that operations and reliability teams can trust. This is a senior cross-organizational leadership role accountable for aligning executive stakeholders, building a high-performing organization, and closing the seams between engineering, procurement, logistics, construction, commissioning, and operations across the estate.

Reports To:
VP, Data Center, Systems Engineering

Direct Reports: Lifecycle Engineering leaders and team

Travel:
Regular travel to data-center sites, supplier factories, and FAT/commissioning activity

Key Responsibilities

Strategy, operating model and investment

Set the enterprise lifecycle engineering strategy and translate it into a costed, sequenced multi-year portfolio roadmap with clear business outcomes, operating-model implications, investment cases, dependencies, and executive decision gates.
Own the lifecycle engineering investment portfolio, business cases and executive-level reporting for CMMS/EAM, Product Information Management (PIM)/ Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), integration, data-platform, and related capabilities; prioritize investment against enterprise risk, scalability, and operational value.
Establish the enterprise lifecycle data governance and design-authority operating model, including domain ownership, stewardship, standards, exceptions, escalation, decision forums, and adoption accountability.
Set and maintain the enterprise target architecture, authoritative-source model, and lifecycle engineering standards so every critical data object has one system of record, one identity, and a controlled route of entry.

Equipment and asset master data and lifecycle

Own the end-to-end equipment and asset data operating model from product definition through procurement, manufacture, logistics, installation, commissioning, handover, maintenance, and reliability.
Establish and enforce canonical equipment and asset identity, taxonomy, hierarchy, naming, units of measure, item-master, configuration, and BOM standards.
Lead data-cleansing, deduplication, and validation-at-source programs that replace unmanaged workbooks and free-text records with governed lifecycle objects and structured exception management.
Set data and document acceptance gates for material readiness, receiving, commissioning completion, and handover into the asset and maintenance environment.

Maintenance, reliability and operational readiness

Own the CMMS/EAM master-data and configuration baseline, including hierarchy, class codes, criticality, PM strategy data, task plans, intervals, labor and skills, parts, closing codes, warranties, and spares.
Establish controlled Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), Method of Procedure (MOP), Emergency Operations Plan (EOP), and libraries linked to asset class, configuration, revision, approval, and point-of-work availability.
Ensure condition data from Data Center Information Management (DCIM), Building Management System (BMS), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), and operational technology systems is deterministically mapped to assets so condition-based maintenance and work orders are trustworthy.
Establish the reliability learning loop across failure coding, bad-actor identification, root-cause analysis, and preventative maintenance optimization so operational learning improves maintenance strategy.

Cross-functional leadership and team development

Serve as the senior accountable escalation point and executive partner for equipment and asset data, lifecycle-readiness, and operating-model disputes across Engineering and Design, Procurement and Supply Chain, Construction and Commissioning, DC Operations and Maintenance, Reliability Engineering, IT, Platform and Data, Finance, and HSE.
Negotiate and enforce supplier and OFCI data and document deliverables, including submittals, FAT evidence, IOMs, serial data, spares, configuration data, and acceptance criteria.
Build, lead, and develop a scalable Lifecycle Engineering organization, including leadership succession, capability planning, talent development, and accountable delivery ownership; set enterprise standards with the Principal Engineer and ensure quality, adoption, and measurable outcomes.
Provide executive and operational leadership through a clear performance system that connects lifecycle engineering investment to PM compliance, MTTR, backlog age, spares fill rate, availability, delivery readiness, and data-quality performance.

Required Experience And Qualifications

15+ years of experience in engineering, asset management, enterprise systems, or a closely related field, including 7+ years leading complex cross-functional systems, data, or operational programs at director, senior-director, or equivalent level.
Proven ownership of a CMMS/EAM platform at scale, such as Attune, IBM Maximo, SAP PM/EAM, Infor EAM, Nuvolo, or equivalent, including master data, PM strategy, work management, and reporting.
Hands-on depth in PIM and/or PLM, configuration management, item master, product variants, BOM structures, engineering change, and effectivity control.
Strong enterprise systems background spanning ERP, procurement and supply-chain systems, document management, integration patterns, and master data governance.
Experience applying ITIL-aligned service management, including change, incident, problem, configuration, and CMDB discipline, to a live operational estate.
Practical experience with controlled SOP, MOP, EOP, LOTO, and permit-to-work regimes in a mission-critical environment.
Experience with Palantir Foundry or an equivalent industrial data platform, and with data stewardship, golden records, validation at source, deduplication, and measurable data-quality KPIs.
Proven responsibility for enterprise strategy, investment governance, organization design, and executive stakeholder management in a complex, high-growth or mission-critical environment.
Demonstrated enterprise leadership ability to set strategy, establish standards, secure adoption, and influence senior leaders across organizational boundaries without direct authority.

Preferred Experience And Qualifications

Data-center plant literacy across electrical and mechanical systems, including UPS, switchgear, transformers, chillers, dry coolers, PDU, busway, BMS/EPMS, and OFCI/CFI delivery models.
Experience integrating DCIM, BMS/SCADA, and OT/IIoT systems, including tag-to-asset mapping and alarm rationalization.
Exposure to reliability engineering methods and standards, including RAM, RCM, FMEA, RCA, ISO 14224, and ISO 55000.
Experience with BIM/COBie handover, digital-twin data exchange, and supplier contract requirements for lifecycle data and documentation.

Technology Leadership

Translate scientific discoveries into scalable commercial solutions that improve product quality, manufacturing capability, and business performance.
Establish the organization as a recognized leader in food science and technology.

Develop compelling customer showcase programs that demonstrate TreeHouse's innovation capabilities.
Create repeatable frameworks for customer ideation sessions, rapid concept development, and collaborative innovation.
Partner closely with Commercial teams to showcase differentiated technologies, product platforms, and innovation pipelines that strengthen customer relationships.

Build enterprise capabilities that serve all business units through shared expertise, best practices, and standardized technical platforms.
Promote collaboration and knowledge sharing across Product Development, Packaging, Operations, Quality, Regulatory, and Commercial teams.
Develop enterprise technical standards that improve consistency, efficiency, and product excellence.

Cultivate a culture of curiosity, learning, and continuous improvement.
Encourage experimentation, external collaboration, and adoption of emerging technologies.

Who We Are

At Firestorm, we are building the future of expeditionary defense manufacturing and autonomous systems. Modern conflict has exposed a fundamental problem: the systems needed most by operators are often too expensive, too slow to produce, and too difficult to sustain at scale. Firestorm exists to change that.

We develop mission-adaptable aerial systems and deployable manufacturing infrastructure designed to put capability directly into the hands of the warfighter. From modular unmanned aircraft to xCell — our deployable microfactory — our goal is to make defense systems rapidly deployable, adaptable, and producible at the point of need.

We are looking for builders, operators, and problem-solvers who want to work on meaningful technology with real-world impact.

About The Role

Firestorm builds uncrewed aircraft and the manufacturing network that produces them: full-capability plants, deployable xCell edge factories, and forward-deployed sites that stand up production near the point of need.

Crucible is the software that runs that network. It plans and executes production across factories that don't look alike, using supply that isn't guaranteed to arrive. It runs in the cloud, inside a factory, and air-gapped in classified environments, with consistent behavior across all three.

Most of what Crucible does has no off-the-shelf solution. Planning has to work across unlike factories and constrained supply. The platform has to operate without cloud or internet access and reconcile correctly when connectivity returns. Export control and audit traceability have to be enforced in the software and data model. The system also has to remain product-agnostic as our aircraft and factories change. The result is a rare combination of distributed systems, manufacturing software, production planning, and real-world operations.

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the team building Crucible. This is a hands-on leadership role with significant ownership: Crucible is early enough that major product and technical decisions are still being made, but mature enough that the software is already being used to run real production. You'll work closely with leadership in Software, Manufacturing, and Product as we scale the Crucible platform and the manufacturing network it serves.

Rippling gives businesses one place to run HR, IT, and Finance. It brings together all of the workforce systems that are normally scattered across a company, like payroll, expenses, benefits, and computers. For the first time ever, you can manage and automate every part of the employee lifecycle in a single system.

Based in San Francisco, CA, Rippling has raised $1.4B+ from the world’s top investors—including Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Sequoia, Greenoaks, and Bedrock—and was named one of America's best startup employers by Forbes.

We prioritize candidate safety. Please be aware that all official communication will only be sent from @Rippling.com addresses.

About The Role

Rippling HRIS is the system of record for employee and organization data and the control plane for the workflows that change it. We’re looking for an Engineering Director to lead the teams responsible for employee transitions, employee terminations, and a new AI-assisted HR workflow charter.

In this role, you will lead a 15-person organization focused on making high-stakes employee lifecycle workflows faster, more reliable, and easier to operate at enterprise scale. You will define the product and technical strategy for AI-assisted workflows that help customers understand employee-change requests, gather missing information, coordinate approvals, and execute approved changes with transparency, human oversight, and auditability.

Why this role exists

Manual to agentic: Employee lifecycle workflows should do more of the work. Today, many processes still depend on an admin knowing the right sequence, collecting context, coordinating stakeholders, and following through manually. The opportunity is to make the product an intelligent partner while preserving human judgment, transparency, and control.
High-stakes product surface: Transition and termination flows touch some of the most consequential employee changes and have downstream effects across HR, payroll, benefits, IT, and finance. The product must make complex cases feel simple without hiding the underlying controls.
Enterprise readiness: Large enterprises bring deeper hierarchies, more policies, fine-grained permissions, global variation, larger bulk operations, and more integrations. The system needs predictable performance, reliability, correctness, and auditability as those dimensions compound.
Unified leadership: A combined 15-person team needs one leader accountable for the product strategy, technical direction, org design, talent bar, and cross-functional operating model across the full charter.

What You Will Do

Transform employee lifecycle workflows from manual to agentic
Define the product and technical strategy for an Agentic HRBP that helps customers reason about, prepare, approve, and execute employee changes.
Move beyond a conversational front end: connect agents to durable workflow execution, company policy, employee context, permissions, approvals, and observable outcomes.
Establish the trust model for high-stakes actions, including clear user intent, human checkpoints where appropriate, explainability, safe failure modes, and complete audit trails.
Create a reusable approach that accelerates new agentic use cases instead of producing one-off demos or brittle automations.
Reach enterprise scale
Make Transition & Termination dependable for large, complex companies across organization structures, employment types, countries, policies, and connected systems.
Raise the bar for performance, availability, correctness, bulk operations, observability, and recovery across synchronous and asynchronous work.
Partner directly with enterprise customers and go-to-market teams to identify the cases that break at scale and translate them into a durable product and platform roadmap.
Modernize the underlying architecture while continuing to deliver customer-facing improvements; sequence the work so the transformation creates leverage rather than a prolonged rewrite.
Build a durable organization
Lead and develop a combined 15-person team, including managers, senior ICs, and emerging leaders as the organization evolves.
Clarify ownership, decision rights, quality bars, and operating rhythms across the Transition & Termination and Agentic HRBP charters.
Hire and retain exceptional talent, raise the leadership bench, and create an environment where product, design, data, AI, and engineering operate as one team.
Represent the charter in company-level planning and make clear trade-offs across near-term customer commitments, foundational investments, and long-term bets.

What You Will Need

Experience as an Engineering Director or equivalent leader overseeing a multi-team product engineering organization.
Experience leading through managers and senior technical leaders, with a track record of developing leadership capacity rather than becoming the decision bottleneck.
Experience owning high-stakes, workflow-heavy products or platforms where correctness, permissions, policy, auditability, and integrations matter.

You will manage all the operational aspects of the software development to ensure business and project objectives are met. You will provide technical, administrative, and people leadership for multiple, diverse, and geographically distributed teams.

You will champion an AI-native approach to software delivery by integrating AI tools, automation, and intelligent engineering workflows across the software development lifecycle to accelerate delivery, improve quality, and increase engineering effectiveness. You will partner closely with product management, enterprise data management, IT, and business stakeholders to align technology delivery with business priorities while meeting healthcare compliance, security, and performance requirements.

This role requires a lead-by-example leader who sets the standard for AI-native engineering and shows teams how modern software delivery can be transformed through AI, automation, and strong technical judgment.

Responsibilities

Leadership & Strategy: Build and lead a multi-team engineering organization with clear goals, outcome-based metrics, and a culture of continuous improvement.
AI-Driven Development: Advance AI-enabled engineering practices by integrating AI tools and automation into workflows with human oversight and clear guardrails.
Technology Alignment: Align teams to enterprise architecture, governance, and shared engineering standards to improve consistency and code quality.
Technical Execution & Oversight: Lead roadmap execution with hands-on technical and architectural oversight to ensure scalable, secure, and maintainable solutions.
Administer budgets, timelines, and performance measures to achieve short- term and long-term objectives for a particular business area.
Instruct, direct, and has oversight responsibility of managers and staff across the Engineering team, working cooperatively with other leaders.
Influence organizational structure within the area of responsibility. Fully responsible for a functional business area and aligns resources to the achievement of business area goals and objectives.

Resource Optimization: Improve delivery throughput and resource utilization through streamlined processes, automation, and AI-enabled tools without compromising quality or maintainability.
Change Management & Influence: As a member of the Technology leadership team, establish and cultivate relationships with business contacts, stakeholders to understand Cotiviti's corporate, business and technology strategies, champion engineering best practices and operational excellence to meet client's needs.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner across Product, Operations, Data, Finance, Security, Program Management and Business teams to translate priorities into engineering plans that deliver measurable outcomes.
Process Improvement & Innovation: Modernize development and testing practices through automation, DevOps, and AI-enabled workflows that improve quality, security, and efficiency.
Talent Development: Recruit, develop, and retain strong engineering talent while building a culture of growth, accountability, and innovation.
Hire, develop, coach, lead and retain top-tier talent, with a focus on building and improving a team and culture that is able to assist in employing best in class practices to support and drive high levels of internal and external customer satisfaction.
Complete all responsibilities as outlined in the annual performance review and/or goal setting.
Complete all special projects and other duties as assigned.
Must be able to perform duties with or without reasonable accommodation.

This job description does not constitute an employment agreement and is subject to change as the needs of Cotiviti and requirements of the job change.

Qualifications

Education & Experience: 10+ years of hands-on experience in software engineering, including 6 years of leading engineering teams as a people manager. Bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field or equivalent; Master’s degree preferred.
Technical Proficiency: Extensive experience designing and delivering complex software systems using Java, React/Angular, microservices, relational and NoSQL databases, cloud platforms, and modern AI-enabled engineering practices, with recent hands-on technical work.
Enterprise Software Delivery: Proven success leading multiple teams and managers to deliver enterprise software across distributed organizations.
Leadership Skills: Strong leadership skills, including building, developing, and mentoring effective engineering teams. Demonstrated experience with managing global development teams.
Adaptive Delivery Models: Strong understanding of Lean, iterative, and flow-based delivery practices that support quality, continuous improvement, and effective execution.
Modern Engineering Practices: Track record of advancing engineering practices through automated testing, TDD, and CI/CD.
Operational & DevOps Knowledge: Solid understanding of software operations and DevOps practices, including reliability, monitoring, telemetry, and incident response.
Problem Solving: Strong problem-solving skills and sound judgment in complex technical environments.
Strategic Execution: Ability to set and execute short- and long-term goals across projects and teams.
Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to diverse stakeholders.
Industry & Compliance: Experience in healthcare or other regulated industries with strong compliance, security, and data privacy requirements is preferred.

Problem-solving and thinking critically.
Completing tasks independently.
Interpreting data.
Making timely decisions in the context of a workflow.
Maintaining focus.
Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned.
Learning new tasks and completing tasks in situations that have a speed or productivity quota.
Remembering and adhering to processes and protocols.

Remaining in a stationary position, often standing or sitting for prolonged periods.
Communicating with others to exchange information.
Repeating motions that may include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers.
Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned.
No adverse environmental conditions expected.
Must be able to provide high-speed internet access / connectivity and office setup and maintenance.
Must be able to provide a dedicated, secure work area.
